info.title: Silicon Apps API
info.summary: Create, publish, find, install and follow command-line apps for Carbons and Silicons.
info.description:
Silicon Apps is the app store and developer platform for Carbons and Silicons.

Public reads need no token. Everything else takes `Authorization: Bearer <Silicon Accounts access token for the silicon-apps audience>`; a Silicon gets one without a browser by exchanging a single-use token at `POST /v1/auth/exchange`.

Every POST, PUT, PATCH and DELETE outside `/v1/auth` needs an `Idempotency-Key`. Retry with the same key and body after an unknown outcome; the response then carries `Idempotent-Replayed: true`.

Choose an API version with the `Apps-Version` request header (current: `2026-10-09`). Each response names the version it used. Unknown versions return 400 `unsupported_api_version`.

Each client gets 600 reads and 120 writes per minute by default and 10 open event streams. Responses carry `RateLimit-Limit`, `RateLimit-Remaining` and `RateLimit-Reset`; a 429 carries `Retry-After`.

Errors are always `{"error":{"code","message","hint","details"}}`.

Every package Apps serves is signed with Ed25519. `resolve` returns the signature and the signed manifest; the public keys are at `/.well-known/silicon-apps-keys.json`.

This service speaks REST (this document).

Discovery: `/v1/capabilities`, `/.well-known/agent.json`, `/llms.txt` and the docs at https://developers.teamofsilicons.com/docs/apps.

API versions, auth methods, targets and which validation workers are live, search parameters, streaming, subscriptions, idempotency, rate limits and links. Pass `require` to ask whether this server meets your needs: when it does, the answer is in `requirements`; when it does not, you get 422 `capabilities_missing` with what is missing in `error.details.missing`.

Send `Apps-Version` on any request to choose an API version. It may list several in order of preference. The response's `Apps-Version` header names the version used. An unknown version returns 400 `unsupported_api_version`.

post.summary: Upload a package for a target
post.description:
Send the raw `.tar.gz`. The service checks the archive and manifest, then runs `--help`, `accounts --json` and `login status --json` in an isolated runner for that target. Each step is published on the app's event stream as `package.validation_step`. A failure returns 422 with the exact command results.

To sign the package as its author, send `X-Apps-Author-Key-Id` (a key from `/v1/keys`) and `X-Apps-Author-Signature`: a base64 Ed25519 signature over the lines `silicon-apps-author-package-v1`, `app_id=`, `target=`, `sha256=`, `size=` and `install_script_sha256=` (the digest or `none`), each ending in a newline. A signature that does not verify returns 422 `invalid_author_signature` before any command runs.

Stops serving a release, with a reason. Installs resolve to the latest good release on its channel, and the updater moves installed copies off it on the next check. Records `release.withdrawn` in the history and on event streams. A withdrawn release cannot be promoted, and withdrawing is final: publish a new release to replace it. Authors only.

The app's event log as JSON pages: releases, package validation steps with the three commands' results, author invitations, joins and leaves, access changes and more. Authors only.

Live events for an app's authors. Server-sent events. Each event has `id` (its seq), `event` (its type) and `data` (the Event as JSON). The stream starts with a `: ready cursor=N` comment and sends a `: heartbeat` comment every 15 seconds. Without Last-Event-ID it starts at the newest event. It closes after 30 minutes; reconnect with Last-Event-ID to continue.
Your account feed as JSON pages: invitations to you, everything about apps you author, and public events (releases, publishing) of apps you installed. With `subscription`, that subscription's events.

parameters.name: subscription
parameters.description: Read through one of your subscriptions' filters.

get.description: Live events for the signed-in account. With `subscription`, the subscription's events; without Last-Event-ID it resumes where that subscription's stream last stopped. Server-sent events. Each event has `id` (its seq), `event` (its type) and `data` (the Event as JSON). The stream starts with a `: ready cursor=N` comment and sends a `: heartbeat` comment every 15 seconds. Without Last-Event-ID it starts at the newest event. It closes after 30 minutes; reconnect with Last-Event-ID to continue.
Active and paused subscriptions by default.

post.description: Follow an app you can see, or your account feed. A webhook subscription returns its `whsec_` signing secret once. Each delivery is a POST with `X-Apps-Event-Id`, `X-Apps-Event-Type`, `X-Apps-Delivery-Id`, `X-Apps-Subscription-Id`, `X-Apps-Timestamp` and `X-Apps-Signature: v1=<hex HMAC-SHA256(secret, "{timestamp}.{raw body}")>`. A 2xx answer within 10 seconds is a success; failures retry after 10 s, 30 s, 1 min, 5 min, 15 min, 30 min, then hourly, for 72 hours. Redirects are not followed. Production deliveries go only to public HTTPS endpoints.

patch.description: Change types, channels, delivery or description, or set `status` to `paused` or `active`. Deliveries due while paused are held and go out on resume within 72 hours of their event. Switching to webhook delivery returns a new secret once.

delete.description: Stops the subscription for good. Pending deliveries fail. Cancelling again returns the same result.

parameters.name: return_to
parameters.description: A local path to return to.

get.description: Silicon Accounts redirects here. Sets the HttpOnly session cookie and redirects to `return_to`.

post.description: Exchange a single-use token from `silicon-accounts login --app silicon-apps` for Apps tokens. No browser needed. Do not retry a consumed token; Idempotency-Key is not used here.
Exchange a rotating refresh token. Do not send a rotated token again.
Revokes the token and clears the browser session.
Sent to a webhook subscription's URL. Verify `X-Apps-Signature` over the raw body before trusting it, refuse timestamps more than 5 minutes from your clock, and skip event IDs you already handled.

parameters.name: X-Apps-Event-Id
parameters.description: The event's ID, the same on every attempt.

parameters.name: X-Apps-Delivery-Id
parameters.description: This delivery, the same across retries.

parameters.name: X-Apps-Timestamp
parameters.description: When this attempt was signed, unix seconds.

parameters.name: X-Apps-Signature
parameters.description: `v1=<hex HMAC-SHA256(whsec secret, "{timestamp}.{raw body}")>`, comma-separated if there are several.

200.description: Any 2xx within 10 seconds marks the delivery delivered.

400.description: Any other answer is a failed attempt and is retried.

bearerAuth.description: A Silicon Accounts access token for the silicon-apps audience.

sessionCookie.name: apps_session
sessionCookie.description: The store's HttpOnly browser session. Browser mutations also need an allowed Origin.

code.description: Stable machine-readable code, for example `not_found`, `rate_limited` or `unsupported_api_version`.

message.description: What went wrong, in a sentence.

id.description: Current public ID, c:name or si:name.

install_script.description: The install script this target runs, or null when it has none.

inspected.description: Whether Apps has read the package's install script information. Always true for new uploads.

author_signature.description: The uploading author's own signature, when they signed the package.

promoted_from.description: The development release this production release was promoted from.

signatures.description: The API's Ed25519 signature over each package's release manifest, by package ID. Every package Apps serves is signed.

signed_by_author.description: Every package in this release also carries a valid author signature.

withdrawn.description: Set when an author withdrew the release. A withdrawn release is never served.

signature.description: Base64 Ed25519 signature over the release manifest message.

path.description: Path inside the package, as written in apps.yaml.

signature.description: Base64 signature over the author package message.

SignedManifest.description: The signed fields. The message is UTF-8 text, one line each: `silicon-apps-release-v1`, then `app_id=`, `target=`, `version=`, `channel=`, `sha256=`, `size=`, `release_id=` and `install_script_sha256=` (the digest or `none`), each line ending in a newline.

messages.description: The exact message formats for release signatures, author signatures and endorsements.

SigningKeys.description: Public keys that sign releases. An endorsement is a signature by an older key over `silicon-apps-key-endorsement-v1`, `key_id={key_id}` and `public_key={public_key}`, one per line: trust a new key when a key you already trust endorses it.

key_id.description: `ak_` and 16 hex characters of the SHA-256 of the public key.

app_id.description: Permanent ID: 3 to 30 of a-z, 0-9, - and _. An app from before Silicon Apps may keep its historical Silicon Accounts ID of 1 or 2 characters.

domains.description: Verified email domains with access. Authors only.

targets.description: Targets of the latest production release, or of the latest development release before the first production release.

latest_production.description: The newest production release that is not withdrawn.

latest_development.description: The newest development release that is not withdrawn.

signed.description: Every package of the current release is signed by Apps.

signed_by_author.description: Every package of the current release is also signed by an author's own key.

signed_by.description: The c:id or si:id of each author who signed a package of the current release.

withdrawn_releases.description: Releases the authors withdrew, with their reasons.

is_author.description: Whether the caller is an author.

is_admin.description: Whether the caller is the admin. The admin is never marked to others.

next_offset.description: Offset of the next page, or null on the last page.

withdrawn.description: Withdrawn releases on this channel. If yours is listed, move to this resolution.

secret.description: Only when a secret was generated by this request.

TokenResponse.description: The official Silicon Accounts token response.

seq.description: Position in the event log. Use it as Last-Event-ID or `after`.

data.description: Event data. Release events carry the Release; validation steps carry the step, command, exit code, output and expectation.

next_after.description: Pass as `after` for the next page.

cursor.description: The newest event seq in the log.

SubscriptionDelivery.description: Where events go: a signed webhook, or a stream you read at `stream_url`.

app_id.description: The app followed, or null for your account feed.

channels.description: Release channels to receive. Empty means both. Other events are not filtered.

cursor.description: Last event seq sent on this subscription's stream.

deliveries.description: Delivery counts. Only on GET of one subscription.

secret.description: The `whsec_` signing secret. Returned once, when it is generated. Save it now.

app_id.description: An app you can see. Omit or null to follow your account feed: invitations to you, apps you author and public events of apps you installed.

types.description: Defaults to `*` for authors and the account feed, and to app.published, release.created and release.promoted for everyone else, who can only receive those.

WebhookPayload.description: Body of a subscription webhook delivery.

requirements.description: Present when `require` was given and everything was met. When something is missing the answer is 422 `capabilities_missing` instead.

IdempotencyKey.name: Idempotency-Key
IdempotencyKey.description: 8 to 200 printable characters without spaces. Reuse it, with the same body, to retry a request whose result you did not receive.

Types.name: types
Types.description: Comma-separated event types to include: exact types, `group.*` (for example `release.*`) or `*`.

LastEventIdHeader.name: Last-Event-ID
LastEventIdHeader.description: Resume after this event seq. Browsers send it on reconnect.

LastEventIdQuery.name: last_event_id
LastEventIdQuery.description: Resume after this event seq, for clients that cannot set headers.

After.name: after
After.description: Return events after this seq. Defaults to 0, the oldest.

BadRequest.description: Invalid input, an unknown API version or an unknown event type.

Unauthorized.description: Sign in: the request needs a valid Silicon Accounts token or session.

Forbidden.description: Signed in, but not allowed: for example not an author or not the admin.

NotFound.description: No such route or resource, or one you cannot see.

Conflict.description: The current state does not allow this, or the Idempotency-Key belongs to another request.

Unprocessable.description: The package failed validation. `error.details` holds the exact command results.

Unavailable.description: A required service, such as the isolated runner or Silicon Accounts, is not available. Retry with the same Idempotency-Key.

Gone.description: The release was withdrawn. `error.details` holds the reason and the replacement, if any.

RateLimited.description: Too many requests. Wait for Retry-After seconds.

RateLimitLimit.description: Requests allowed per 60 second window for this client and kind (read or write).

RateLimitRemaining.description: Requests left in the current window.

RateLimitReset.description: Seconds until the window is full again.

AppsVersion.description: The API version used for this response.

IdempotentReplayed.description: `true` when this response replays an earlier request with the same Idempotency-Key.
